threads.thread_goal: Align on final tier structure, benefits, and pricing before documentation freeze.

messages.text: Sharing the latest draft of the tier structure in the Tiered Membership Design Specification now, covering three tiers and initial pricing bands. Before I lock this into A1 for the Launch of Tiered Membership Program for Key Customer Segments, can you review the eligibility rules and benefit groupings, especially how they connect to the operations flows in A3 and the scope of T1 and T3. I have kept it to three tiers to avoid confusion, but I am not fully sure about the naming and whether the price gaps are strong enough. Looking for your input on both the names and the price anchors before we freeze.

Thanks for sending this over. I have gone through the A1 draft and the three tiers feel like the right number from a sales perspective. The current names are a bit generic though, which might make it harder for the team to position the value difference quickly. Could we try names that signal progression more clearly, for example something like a base tier focused on essentials, a mid tier that highlights growth, and a top tier that signals priority treatment. On pricing, the gaps between tiers look narrow in the mid to top jump, which might reduce upsell leverage. I would suggest we model a slightly wider spread and check with finance on margin impact before we finalize T1.

I have also reviewed the A1 draft. From an operations and service angle, the three tiers are manageable, and they map reasonably well to the flows we are sketching in A3 for onboarding and upgrades under T3. One concern is that some benefits in the mid tier overlap heavily with the top tier, which might create confusion when we explain upgrades or downgrades. It could help to make at least one or two benefits clearly exclusive to the top tier, so that the upgrade path is easier to explain in scripts and in the playbook.

Good points on both naming and pricing. I had kept the names simple to avoid confusion, but I see the risk that they do not help the sales team tell a clear story. I can rework the names to show a clearer progression, and I will widen the price gap between the mid and top tiers as you suggest. I will need support to check the margin impact though, so I will prepare a short summary and ask finance to validate before we close T1. Once we have that, I will update A1 accordingly.

Agree on the need for clearer differentiation at the top tier. From a sales conversation point of view, we need one or two standout benefits that are only available at the highest tier, otherwise the team will struggle to justify the higher price. Maybe we can move one of the more premium service elements you listed in A3 for special handling into the top tier only, and keep the mid tier focused on a smaller set of strong but more standard benefits. That would also make it easier to reflect in the sales pitch work under T2 later.

If we adjust the benefits so that the top tier has one or two exclusive items, I can help make sure the operations playbook in A3 reflects the extra handling steps. For example, if we add priority support or a dedicated contact, we will need to define how that is triggered in the process flows under T3 and how we tag those members in the system later under T4. That way, the service team will not be surprised at launch.

I had a quick look at A1 as well. One thing I am not fully clear on is how strict the eligibility rules should be between tiers. For example, can any existing member move straight to the top tier, or do they need to meet some minimum criteria first. I am asking because this will affect how we explain upgrades and downgrades in the FAQ and in the operations playbook. If we keep it simple, it might be easier for the teams to follow, but I am not sure if that creates any risk for margins.

On eligibility, my suggestion is to keep the rules simple but still anchored in clear criteria, such as spend or tenure, so that we can explain them easily and avoid disputes. For example, we could allow any member to buy into the mid tier, but reserve the top tier for members who meet a minimum spend or are invited based on a review. That would help protect margins and also create a sense of exclusivity. We should check with finance and legal on any constraints, but this structure has worked well in similar programs I have seen.

That makes sense. I will draft eligibility rules along those lines in A1, with a simple spend or tenure threshold for the top tier and more open access to the mid tier. I will also flag this to finance and legal for a quick review so we do not run into issues later. Once I have their feedback, I will update the draft and share a short summary here before we freeze T1.

When you update A1 with the new eligibility rules and benefit split, could you also highlight any changes that impact the lifecycle flows in A3. That will help me and the rest of the team adjust the onboarding, upgrade, and downgrade steps under T3 without missing anything. In particular, we should check how downgrades from the top tier will work if someone no longer meets the criteria, so that we have a clear process and communication plan.

I have run a quick sense check on the revised pricing bands you proposed in the updated A1 draft. The wider gap between mid and top tiers looks reasonable from a sales standpoint and should support upsell conversations. As long as finance confirms that the benefits package remains margin positive within the six month window, I am comfortable moving ahead. From my side, I am ready to align the sales pitch work in T2 to this structure.

Finance has now confirmed that the revised pricing and benefit mix in A1 stays within the margin targets, assuming we monitor usage closely in the first months. Given that, and the feedback here, I propose that we confirm three tiers as the final structure and proceed with the updated naming convention that signals progression clearly. Unless there are strong objections today, I will treat this as our final call for T1 and move A1 to a stable version for the rest of the work.

No objections from my side. Three tiers with the updated names work well for the sales story, and the eligibility rules and pricing bands in A1 are clear enough for the team to apply. For the benefits, I suggest we lock the core list now so that we can start drafting the sales pitch and objection handling in A2 without rework. We can still fine tune smaller details later, but the main structure should stay stable.

I am aligned as well. The three tier structure and the clarified benefit split give us enough clarity to move forward with the operations playbook in A3 under T3. I will start mapping the onboarding and change flows to these tiers and call out any operational constraints, but I do not see anything that would block us from locking the core benefits and pricing bands now.

I am ok with the three tiers and the updated names as well. The eligibility rules in A1 are now clearer for me, especially the criteria for the top tier. For the benefits, I just want to confirm that the FAQ and escalation content later in A8 will reflect the final list, so that front line teams have a single source of truth. As long as we keep that in sync, I am comfortable with locking the core benefits and pricing bands.

To make it explicit for everyone, I suggest we record that the final list of core benefits per tier and the pricing bands in A1 are now approved for launch design. Any further changes should be treated as exceptions and checked with finance and operations. This will help us keep T1 and T3 on track and avoid last minute shifts that could confuse the sales and service teams.

Agreed. I will mark the current A1 draft as the baseline for the three tiers, including the approved names, eligibility rules, core benefits, and pricing bands. Any further adjustments will go through a short review with finance and sales before we update the document. This should give everyone a stable reference for the operations playbook in A3 and the rest of the tasks linked to T1 and T3.

threads.thread_goal: Lock sales pitch, objection handling, and training approach for launch.

messages.text: I have uploaded the first full draft of the sales pitch and objection handling content into A2, based on the approved tier structure in A1 and the scope of T2. The draft includes a standard pitch flow for each tier and a list of the top objections we expect from existing members. I have also sketched a training outline under T5 that links to the launch communication plan in A5. Please review and let me know if anything feels too complex or misaligned with the operations playbook.

I have gone through the A2 draft. The overall structure is clear, and I like that the pitch starts from member needs rather than features. One area I am unsure about is the level of detail in the objection handling section. Some of the responses are quite long, which might be hard for the team to remember. Could we simplify a few of them into shorter key phrases, while keeping the full explanation in the background material. Also, for the training outline in T5, I want to make sure we can fit the sessions into the teams schedules within the 21 day window.

From the operations side, the pitch in A2 lines up with the flows we are drafting in A3, especially around upgrades and downgrades. One thing I would add is a short reminder in the script about checking eligibility and data fields before promising a benefit, so that we avoid mismatches with what is actually configured in the system. That will also support the data standards work under T4. On training, it would help if we include a short segment on how to handle edge cases and when to escalate.

I have a question on the training outline in T5. Are we expecting all sales and membership staff to attend the same full session, or will there be shorter refreshers for some groups. I am asking because some team members might struggle to attend a long session in one go. Also, for the objection list in A2, could we add a few examples related to members who are worried about losing existing benefits when they move tiers.

Good call on simplifying the objection responses. I can rework the A2 content so that each objection has a short headline response plus a few supporting points, and keep the longer explanation in the notes. That should make it easier for the team to remember. On the training schedule for T5, my proposal is to run one core session that is mandatory for all front line staff, and then offer shorter optional clinics focused on more complex scenarios. We will need to confirm this split together.

I will add a clear step in the pitch flow in A2 that reminds the rep to confirm eligibility and data fields before committing to a benefit, and reference the tagging rules from A4 once they are finalized. For training under T5, we can include a short module on edge cases and escalation, using examples from the operations playbook in A3 and the FAQ work in A8. That should help reduce confusion at launch.

I like the idea of one core mandatory session plus optional clinics. That should help us balance consistency with flexibility. From my side, I would suggest that the core session covers the tier structure from A1, the standard pitch from A2, and the key process points from A3. The optional clinics can then go deeper into objection handling and special cases. We just need to be clear in T5 and A5 which sessions are mandatory so that team leads can plan attendance.

I have reviewed the pitch flow in A2 from a field sales perspective. The structure is strong, but I would recommend we add a simple opening question set to quickly identify which tier is most relevant for the member, so that the conversation does not feel scripted. Also, for the objection list, we might want to include a few points about price sensitivity and how to steer members towards the mid tier when the top tier is not a fit. This will be important for the teams that work with more price conscious segments.

Great input. I will add a short discovery question block at the start of the pitch in A2, focused on needs and current usage, to help the rep decide which tier to lead with. For price sensitivity, I will include a couple of objection examples that show how to position the mid tier as a strong value option without undermining the top tier. This will be reflected in the T2 deliverable and reinforced during training.

On the training split, I support having one core session that everyone attends. For the optional clinics, could we record them and share the links in A5 so that people who cannot join live can still catch up. That might also help new joiners after launch. For the objection list in A2, thanks for adding the examples about members worried about losing benefits, that will be very useful for the team.

I have now updated A2 with the simplified objection responses, the eligibility check step, and the discovery questions. The training outline in T5 and the related section in A5 now specify one mandatory core session for all sales and membership staff, plus two optional clinics focused on advanced objection handling and complex scenarios. Unless there are concerns, I would like to confirm this as our standard pitch framework and training approach so we can move into scheduling.

From my side, the updated A2 looks solid and aligned with the tier design in A1 and the operations flows in A3. I am comfortable treating this as the standard pitch framework for launch. The training split in T5 also works for the membership teams, as long as we get the dates into calendars soon. I suggest we proceed with scheduling and use A5 to track attendance and any follow up needs.

I am aligned as well. The framework in A2 is clear enough for the field teams, and the combination of one mandatory core session plus optional clinics in T5 should give us the right balance. I will work with team leads to make sure attendance is prioritized, and we can use feedback from the first sessions to fine tune the examples if needed.

Thanks all. I will treat the current A2 as the approved standard for the sales pitch and objection handling, and the training plan in T5 and A5 as final for scheduling. I will coordinate with team leads to lock dates and share invites, and we will monitor attendance and feedback closely as part of the launch readiness checks.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on data fields, tagging rules, and pre-launch data clean-up scope.

messages.text: I have shared an initial version of the Membership Data Fields and Tagging Matrix in A4, along with a short summary of the data audit findings from T8. The proposal covers required fields for the new tiers, tagging rules for segments, and some suggested clean up actions before launch. Please review and let me know if any key fields are missing for sales or service, and which clean up items you think we must complete before go live versus later.

I have gone through A4 and the T8 summary. The core fields for tier, segment, and consent status look right from a sales perspective. I would suggest we add a simple flag for members who have been contacted about the new program, so that we can avoid duplicate outreach and track follow up. On clean up, I think we should prioritize fixing missing contact details and inconsistent tier tags, as these will directly impact targeting and reporting in the first weeks.

From the membership operations side, the fields in A4 cover most of what we need to run the processes in A3. I would like to confirm that we have a clear way to record upgrade and downgrade dates, as this will be important for service teams when handling complaints or questions. For the clean up actions in T8, I agree we should focus on missing contact details and tier tags before launch, and leave some of the older historical data issues for later phases.

I have a question about the consent fields in A4. Are we planning to store separate flags for different communication channels, or just one overall consent status. I want to make sure we do not create confusion for the teams when they check if they can contact a member. Also, for the clean up tasks in T8, do we have enough capacity to fix all the missing data before launch, or should we narrow the scope.

On consent, my recommendation is to keep separate flags for at least email and phone, as this will matter for the launch communication plan in A5 and for follow up calls. We can still present it simply in the interface so that teams see a clear yes or no per channel. Regarding clean up scope, I agree we should be realistic. If we focus on target segments for the pilot and early launch, we can get the most impact from the T8 work without overloading the team.

Thanks for the feedback. I will add a contact history flag to A4 so we can track who has been approached about the new tiers. For the clean up actions in T8, I will mark missing contact details and inconsistent tier tags as must do before launch, and we can treat older historical issues as a later improvement. I will also check with the data team to confirm what is feasible in the next two weeks.

For upgrade and downgrade dates, we can add two date fields in A4 and make them required whenever a tier change is processed in the operations flows in A3. That will give us a clear history for service teams and for reporting later. We should also include a short note in the pre launch readiness checklist in A6 to confirm that these fields are correctly configured and visible to front line staff.

Looking at A4 from a sales reporting angle, I would like to ensure we have fields that allow us to track which tier was pitched and which tier was chosen, so we can see conversion patterns. This might be as simple as a field for recommended tier and a field for final tier. It will help us refine the pitch and incentives later. For clean up, I support focusing on the segments we will target first, as mentioned in the T8 summary.

I will update A4 to include separate consent flags for email and phone, plus the contact history flag and the upgrade and downgrade dates. I will also add fields for recommended tier and final tier as suggested. Once that is done, we should confirm that this set of fields is final so that the data and IT teams can configure the system without further changes. For T8, I will refine the clean up list to focus on target segments and the must do items we have identified.

With these additions, the field set in A4 looks complete from my side. It covers what we need for targeting, consent, and sales reporting. I suggest we formally confirm this as the final list of required membership data fields for launch, so that we can move ahead with configuration and avoid late changes that could delay us.

Agreed. Let us record that the current A4 matrix, including the consent flags, contact history, upgrade and downgrade dates, and recommended versus final tier fields, is our final set of required data fields for launch. I will communicate this to the data and IT teams as the baseline for T4. Any further changes will need a clear justification and sign off.

On the clean up scope in T8, I recommend we mark the following as in scope before launch in the A6 checklist: fixing missing contact details for target segments, correcting inconsistent tier tags, and updating consent flags where we have clear records. Items like older inactive members and minor formatting issues can be handled after launch. This should keep the workload manageable while still protecting the quality of our launch targeting.

I support that prioritization. Those three clean up items will have the biggest impact on our ability to reach the right members and measure results. We can document the rest as post launch improvements. I suggest we formally agree that these are the in scope clean up actions for T8 before launch, so that the data team can plan their work accordingly.

Let us capture that decision clearly. For T8, the in scope pre launch clean up actions are: fixing missing contact details for target segments, correcting inconsistent tier tags, and updating consent flags where we have reliable records. Other issues will be tracked as post launch items in A6. I will share this scope with the data team and include it in the next launch readiness review.

threads.thread_goal: Define pilot scope, success criteria, and adjustments before full rollout.

messages.text: I have drafted a proposal for the pilot in line with T10 and shared a short outline in the Pilot Results and Recommendations Report template A7. The idea is to run a four week pilot with a small group of existing members across two key segments, using the full three tier structure and the operations flows from A3. Please review the suggested cohort size, duration, and feedback collection approach, and let me know if you see any risks or gaps before we lock the scope.

I have reviewed the pilot outline. A four week duration feels reasonable to capture initial reactions and some early usage patterns. On cohort size, I would suggest we keep it focused but large enough to see differences between tiers, maybe a few hundred members per segment rather than a very small sample. We should also define clear success criteria, such as upgrade rates, member satisfaction, and complaint levels, so that A7 can give us a solid basis for adjustments before full launch.

From an operations standpoint, running the pilot across two segments is manageable as long as we have clear guidance in A3 and the FAQ in A8 for the teams involved. We should make sure the pilot cohort is clearly tagged in the system so that we can track their interactions and avoid mixing them with non pilot members. Also, we need to include pilot readiness checks in A6 so that we do not miss any configuration steps.

Looking at this from the sales side, I would recommend we involve a mix of more experienced and newer reps in the pilot, so that we can see how the pitch and objection handling from A2 work across different profiles. For cohort size, I agree with keeping it to a few hundred per segment. We should also plan short check ins during the pilot to capture qualitative feedback from the teams, not just the numbers in A7.

I have a question about how we will collect member feedback during the pilot. Are we planning surveys, calls, or both. I want to make sure we do not overload members but still get enough insight to adjust the FAQ and escalation matrix in A8. Also, will the pilot members keep their new tier after the pilot, or could they be moved back if we change the structure.

For feedback, I would suggest a combination of a short survey after the first interaction plus a small number of follow up calls for deeper insight. That should give us enough input for A7 without overwhelming members. On whether pilot members keep their tier, my preference is that any upgrades they receive remain in place, even if we tweak details later, to avoid negative reactions. We can design the pilot so that we do not promise anything we cannot sustain.

Based on the feedback, I will adjust the pilot proposal to target a few hundred members per segment, across two key segments, for four weeks. I will also define success criteria in A7 around upgrade rates, satisfaction scores, and complaint levels, plus a simple operational stability measure. We will tag the pilot cohort clearly in the system and include pilot specific checks in A6. Once updated, I will share the revised outline for final confirmation.

Please also specify in A3 which teams and channels are in scope for the pilot, so that we can brief them properly and avoid confusion in other areas. For A6, we can add a line to confirm that pilot members are correctly tagged and that the FAQ and escalation paths in A8 are available to the pilot teams before we start.

On success criteria, I would add a simple metric on how comfortable reps feel with the pitch and processes, maybe through a short internal survey during the pilot. This will help us see if the training and materials are sufficient or if we need more support before full rollout. We can include this in A7 as a qualitative indicator.

I have now updated the pilot outline to reflect two key segments, a few hundred members per segment, and a four week duration. The in scope teams and channels are listed in A3, and the success criteria in A7 include upgrade rates, satisfaction, complaints, operational stability, and rep confidence. Unless there are objections, I propose we approve this pilot cohort size, duration, and segment selection as the basis for T10.

I am aligned with the updated pilot scope. The cohort size and duration should give us enough data without putting too much strain on the teams. For adjustments before full rollout, I suggest we agree that any major changes recommended in A7, such as altering benefits or pricing, must be applied before full launch, while smaller tweaks to scripts or training can be phased in during the first weeks.

That approach makes sense. From an operations view, we should definitely apply any changes from A7 that affect core processes or member promises before full launch, so that we do not confuse staff or members. Smaller adjustments to wording in scripts or FAQs can be rolled out after launch as long as they are tracked. We can capture this rule in the launch readiness checklist in A6.

Let us formalize that. For A7, any recommendations that change the tier structure, benefits, pricing, or core eligibility rules will be applied before full launch. Recommendations that only adjust scripts, training examples, or minor process wording can be scheduled for the early post launch period. We will reflect this in A6 so that it is clear during readiness reviews.

With that, I think we have a clear pilot scope and a rule for which changes from A7 must be in place before full rollout. I will make sure the sales teams involved in the pilot are briefed on the success criteria and feedback channels, so that we get strong input for the final adjustments.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize cross-team launch timeline, KPIs, and review cadence.

messages.text: I have put together a draft cross team launch timeline in line with T11 and shared it in the Launch Communication and Training Plan A5. It maps the remaining design work, training under T5, the pilot from T10, and the full launch, along with key checkpoints from the Pre Launch Readiness Checklist A6. Please review the milestones and dependencies and let me know if anything looks unrealistic or missing.

I have reviewed the timeline in A5. The overall sequence makes sense, with design freeze, training, pilot, and then full launch. One adjustment I would suggest is to bring the first training sessions slightly earlier, so that the teams involved in the pilot are fully prepared before it starts. We should also add the weekly performance review cadence from T12 to the post launch section, with clear dates for the first two meetings.

From the operations side, the milestones in A5 align with what we need for the playbook in A3 and the data work in A4. I would just highlight that we need at least a few days between finalizing the operations playbook and the start of training, so that we can incorporate any last feedback. Also, it would be good to include a specific checkpoint in A6 to confirm that escalation paths and FAQs in A8 are ready before full launch.

Looking at the sales related milestones, I think we should also include a step to align sales targets and incentive rules under T9 before full launch, so that the teams know how the new tiers will be reflected in their goals. This should happen after we have pilot insights but before we communicate final targets. We can add this as a milestone in A5 with a dependency on the pilot results in A7.

I will adjust the timeline in A5 so that the first core training sessions under T5 happen before the pilot starts, with enough time for follow up questions. I will also add the weekly performance review meetings from T12 into the post launch section, including the first two dates. For A6, I will make sure these checkpoints are reflected so that we track them in the readiness reviews.

Good point on T9. I will add a milestone in A5 for defining sales targets and incentive rules after we have the pilot results in A7, with enough time to review with finance. This will ensure that the teams have clarity on how the new tiers affect their goals before full launch. We can also include a brief update on this in the first weekly performance review under T12.

I have a question about the KPIs we will track in the weekly performance reviews under T12. Are we focusing only on uptake and revenue, or will we also track complaints and service metrics. It would be helpful for the membership teams to see both, so that we can react quickly if members are confused or unhappy with the new tiers.

For the weekly reviews, my proposal is to track a small set of core KPIs: new sign ups by tier, upgrades and downgrades, revenue contribution, and a few service indicators such as complaints related to the program and average resolution time. We can also include a simple satisfaction measure if we have survey data. I will document this KPI set in the T12 deliverable and reference it in A5 and A6.

Including complaints and resolution time in the core KPIs will be very helpful for the membership and service teams. We should also make sure that any recurring issues identified in these reviews are fed back into updates to A3 and A8. Maybe we can add a short standing agenda item in the T12 meeting format for operational issues and member feedback.

I have now updated A5 with the adjusted training dates, pilot timing, the T9 milestone, and the weekly review cadence from T12. The A6 checklist has been refreshed to include checks for training completion, pilot configuration, FAQ and escalation readiness, and KPI reporting setup. Please take a final look and confirm that this integrated timeline and review cadence works for your teams.

From the sales side, the updated timeline and KPIs look good. The sequence of design freeze, training, pilot, target and incentive definition, and full launch is clear, and the weekly review cadence under T12 should give us enough visibility to react quickly. I am comfortable moving forward with this plan as our cross team baseline.

I am aligned as well. The added milestone for T9 and the inclusion of KPIs that cover both sales and service give us a balanced view. The first two review dates in T12 are workable for the field teams, and we can adjust participation if needed once we see how the meetings run.

From the membership operations perspective, the timeline and checkpoints in A5 and A6 are clear and achievable. The spacing between finalizing A3 and the start of training gives us enough time to incorporate feedback. I am fine with using this as the final integrated plan.

Thanks everyone. I will treat the current A5 timeline and KPI set as the agreed cross team plan for T11 and T12. We will use A6 to track readiness against these milestones and adjust only if we hit unexpected constraints. I will circulate a brief summary to stakeholders so that everyone is aligned on dates and review cadence.
